# KM-104 — M1 contracts module

**Lane:** app · **Complexity:** 1 · **Model:** codex · **Depends on:** none · **Serializes with:** none (KM-170 later adds `packages/contracts/src/m1/channel-event.ts` to the same folder; it depends on this ticket)
**Plan context (pinned):** [M1 plan](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/plans/2026-10-01-002-refactor-external-m1-thin-path-plan.md) · [contracts](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/contracts.md) · [roster and graph](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/roster.md)
**Exclusive write surfaces:** `packages/contracts/src/m1/{agent-join,participants,inbox}.ts`, `packages/contracts/src/m1/{agent-join,participants,inbox}.test.ts`, `packages/contracts/package.json` (the `exports` map only)

## Outcome

`@khala/contracts/m1/agent-join`, `@khala/contracts/m1/participants` and `@khala/contracts/m1/inbox` exist and export the C2, C3 and C5 types exactly as written in contracts.md. Each module also exports small strict runtime decoders. Control (KM-122, KM-131, KM-132), web (KM-134, KM-135) and the agent (KM-141, KM-142, KM-144, KM-145) import one shared definition instead of re-declaring shapes.

## Context and evidence

- contracts.md C1: every wire and record type lives at `@khala/contracts/m1/<module>` in the new folder `packages/contracts/src/m1/`.
- Plan KTD3 (join handshake), KTD6 (inbox), KTD9 (owner map), U10, U12, U15.
- The package exports source `.ts` through wildcard subpaths: `packages/contracts/package.json:6-10` (`"./messaging/*": "./src/messaging/*.ts"`). Consumers import without an extension, for example `'@khala/contracts/messaging/index'`.
- The decode style to follow is `packages/contracts/src/messaging/decode.ts`. Decoders take `unknown`, never coerce or drop fields, throw `DecodeFailure` through `fail()`, and are wrapped by `decodeWith()` into `Decoded<T>`. A worked union example that reads a discriminant before `object()` is `decodePersonalChannelLinkResult` at `packages/contracts/src/messaging/channel-link.ts:63-82`.
- C2 says the label follows "validateAgentName rules". That function is `packages/contracts/src/messaging/agent-names.ts:12-20`. It trims, applies NFC, rejects unsafe characters and reserved words (`khala`, `owner`, `system`, …), and caps at 80 UTF-8 bytes.
- `scripts/check-boundaries.mjs:130-131`: contracts may import only contracts. Contracts graphs must stay pure, so no `node:` imports (`:150-152`).
- `tsconfig.base.json` sets `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. An optional field must be omitted, never set to `undefined`.

## Contract and invariants

Quote these verbatim in the modules. Do not rename fields, add `Readonly<>` or add fields.

C2 (`agent-join.ts`):

```ts
export type Harness = 'claude' | 'codex';
export type AgentJoinRequest = { link: string; harness: Harness; label: string };   // label 1..40 chars, validateAgentName rules
export type AgentJoinCreated = { joinId: string; pollSecret: string; confirmUrl: string; expiresAt: string }; // 201
export type AgentJoinPoll =
  | { state: 'pending' }
  | { state: 'confirmed'; credentials: AgentCredentials }   // returned exactly once
  | { state: 'claimed' }                                     // credentials already taken
  | { state: 'expired' };
export type AgentCredentials = {
  homeserver: string;      // e.g. "https://127.0.0.1:8443" locally
  userId: string;          // "@agent-1a2b3c4d-x9y8z7:khala.local"
  accessToken: string;
  deviceId: string;        // "KH_AGENT_<uuid8>"
  roomId: string;          // the channel's Matrix room id
};
export type AgentJoinView = { joinId: string; label: string; harness: Harness; channelName: string; roomId: string;
  state: 'pending' | 'confirmed' | 'ready' | 'expired'; agentUserId?: string };
```

C2 preamble (verbatim, as amended in contracts.md on 2026-10-01):

> - **Exact paths only.** The control gateway matches exact paths (`apps/control/src/runtime/handler.ts:9-14`), so `joinId` always travels as a query parameter, never as a path segment.
> - **Origin header.** Every agent-client POST sends `Origin: <app origin>`, the origin of the channel link. The gateway rejects a POST whose Origin is foreign (`apps/control/src/auth/csrf.ts:14-20`).
> - **Confirm URL.** The `confirmUrl` is `<app origin>/agent/confirm?joinId=<joinId>`.

C2 routes:
- `POST /api/agent/join`
- `GET /api/agent/join/poll?joinId=<joinId>`
- `POST /api/agent/join/ready?joinId=<joinId>`
- `GET /api/human/agent-join?joinId=<joinId>`
- `POST /api/human/agent-join/confirm?joinId=<joinId>`
- `GET /api/human/agent-join/status?joinId=<joinId>`

C4 (verbatim):

> `ownerFirstName` is derived from the owner's verified email. Take the first `.`, `_`, `-` or `+`-separated token of the local part, strip trailing digits and capitalise it; if the result is empty, use `Owner`. Example: `kevin.weaver2@gmail.com` → `Kevin`. KM-122, KM-132 and KM-135 use this same rule via `ownerFirstName(email)` exported from `packages/contracts/src/m1/participants.ts`, which KM-104 owns.
> - **Human labels come from Matrix display names, everywhere.** When KM-122 mints a browser session, it sets the human's own Matrix display name to `ownerFirstName(verifiedEmail)`: read it first, write only if different. Readers (control participants, browser, KM-143 agent intake) use the display name. Fallback when it is missing: control's participants `displayName` falls back to the full `matrixUserId` (C3); KM-143's `senderLabel` falls back to the user id localpart.

Error codes in C2: `400 invalid_link | invalid_label | invalid_harness ; 404 link_unavailable ; 429 rate_limited`, `404 not_found`, `409 not_confirmed`, `401 signed_out ; 403 not_member ; 404 not_found`, `409 already_confirmed_by_other`. Errors are `{ "error": <code> }`.

C3 (`participants.ts`), Blobs key `agents/<encodeURIComponent(matrixUserId)>`:

```ts
export type AgentOwnerRecord = { matrixUserId: string; ownerId: string; ownerLabel: string; harness: Harness; label: string; createdAt: string };
```

> Participants: there is **no new route**. The existing `POST /api/human/messaging/participants` (`apps/control/src/composition/human/handlers.ts:31`, `:352-388` at `5db209cc`) keeps its request shape (`{ userIds, roomId?, deviceId?, matrixAccessToken?, targetParticipantIds? }`). Each entry of its `{ participants: [...] }` response keeps today's keys and gains `kind: 'human'|'agent'|'unknown'`, plus `ownerLabel` and `harness` when `kind === 'agent'`:

```ts
export type Participant =
  | { matrixUserId: string; participantId: string; ownerId: string; displayName: string; kind: 'human' }
  | { matrixUserId: string; participantId: string; ownerId: string; displayName: string; kind: 'agent'; ownerLabel: string; harness: Harness }
  | { matrixUserId: string; displayName: string; kind: 'unknown' };   // an unknown member never fails the whole response
export type ParticipantsResponse = { participants: Participant[] };
```

> - `displayName` is the member's Matrix display name (C4 human-label rule), falling back to `matrixUserId`.

C5 (`inbox.ts`): `InboxEntry` exactly as in contracts.md C5 (`packages/contracts/src/m1/inbox.ts` block), keeping the field comments.

Invariants:
- Every decoder rejects unknown and missing keys, because `object()` enforces exact keys.
- No decoder trims or normalises. A label that `validateAgentName` would change, for example `" Claude"`, is rejected, not repaired.
- Room ids are checked only as `!` followed by non-whitespace. Room version 12 ids have no `:server` part.

### Exports (exact names)

`agent-join.ts`, besides the C2 types:
- `HARNESSES = ['claude', 'codex'] as const`, `AGENT_LABEL_MAX_CHARS = 40`, `M1_LABEL_MAX_BYTES = 512` and `CHANNEL_LINK_MAX_BYTES = 2048`.
- `type AgentJoinErrorCode`: the union of the ten C2 codes above. `type AgentJoinError = { error: AgentJoinErrorCode }`.
- Path helpers that mirror the amended C2 exactly. `joinId` is always a query parameter, encoded with `encodeURIComponent`:
  - `AGENT_JOIN_PATH = '/api/agent/join'`
  - `agentJoinPollPath(id)` → `/api/agent/join/poll?joinId=<id>`
  - `agentJoinReadyPath(id)` → `/api/agent/join/ready?joinId=<id>`
  - `humanAgentJoinPath(id)` → `/api/human/agent-join?joinId=<id>`
  - `humanAgentJoinConfirmPath(id)` → `/api/human/agent-join/confirm?joinId=<id>`
  - `humanAgentJoinStatusPath(id)` → `/api/human/agent-join/status?joinId=<id>`
  - `agentConfirmPagePath(id)` → `/agent/confirm?joinId=<id>` (the `confirmUrl` is `<app origin>` + this)
- Readers, which throw through `fail`:
  - `readHarness(input, path)`: `literal` over `HARNESSES`.
  - `readAgentLabel(input, path)`: string; `validateAgentName(input)` is ok and `.name === input`; `[...input].length <= 40`. Otherwise `fail(path, 'invalid_value')`. A non-string fails with `'wrong_type'`.
  - `readChannelLink(input, path)`:
    - string, at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes, and `new URL()` parses it;
    - `url.href === input`;
    - protocol `https:`, or `http:` with host `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`;
    - no username, password, search or hash;
    - pathname matches `/^\/join\/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,256}$/u`.
  - `readMatrixUserId(input, path)`: `identifier` and `/^@[^\s:]+:\S+$/u`.
  - `readRoomId(input, path)`: `identifier` and `/^!\S+$/u`.
  - `readHttpUrl(input, path)`: same protocol and loopback rule as `readChannelLink`, with no userinfo or hash.
- Decoders, each `(input: unknown) => Decoded<T>`:
  - `decodeAgentJoinRequest` and `decodeAgentJoinCreated`. In `AgentJoinCreated`:
    - `joinId` and `pollSecret` use `identifier`;
    - `expiresAt` uses `utcTimestamp`;
    - `confirmUrl` uses `readHttpUrl`, then must satisfy all of `url.pathname === '/agent/confirm'`, `[...url.searchParams.keys()]` equal to `['joinId']`, and `url.searchParams.get('joinId') === joinId`. Otherwise `fail('confirmUrl', 'invalid_value')`.
  - `decodeAgentCredentials`. `homeserver` is `readHttpUrl` with `new URL(v).origin === v`. `userId` is `readMatrixUserId`. `accessToken` and `deviceId` are `identifier`. `roomId` is `readRoomId`.
  - `decodeAgentJoinPoll`: read `state` first, as `channel-link.ts:65` does, then `object()` with `['state','credentials']` for `confirmed` and `['state']` otherwise.
  - `decodeAgentJoinView`: call `object()` with the six required keys plus `'agentUserId'` only when `Object.hasOwn(input, 'agentUserId')`; read it with `readMatrixUserId` and omit the key from the result otherwise. `channelName` uses `label(…, 512)` and may be empty.
  - `decodeAgentJoinError`.
- `agentJoinRequestErrorCode(error: DecodeError): 'invalid_label' | 'invalid_harness' | 'invalid_link'`. A path starting with `label` maps to `invalid_label`, `harness` to `invalid_harness`, and everything else (including root `not_object` and `unknown_field`) to `invalid_link`.

`participants.ts`:
- C3 types; `import type { Harness } from './agent-join'`.
- `MAX_PARTICIPANTS = 100`.
- `agentOwnerRecordKey(matrixUserId)` → `` `agents/${encodeURIComponent(matrixUserId)}` ``. KM-122 reads this key and KM-132 writes it.
- `ownerFirstName(email: string): string`, implementing the C4 rule exactly:
  1. The local part is the text before the last `@`, or the whole string when there is no `@`.
  2. The token is `local.split(/[._+-]/u)[0] ?? ''`.
  3. Strip trailing digits with `.replace(/\d+$/u, '')`.
  4. Uppercase the first character and leave the rest unchanged.
  5. An empty result gives `'Owner'`.
- `decodeAgentOwnerRecord`:
  - `ownerId` uses `identifier`;
  - `ownerLabel` uses `label(…, 512)`, and the result must not be empty;
  - `label` uses `readAgentLabel`;
  - `createdAt` uses `utcTimestamp`.
- `decodeParticipant`: read `kind` first (as `channel-link.ts:65` does), then `object()` with exact keys: `human` → `['matrixUserId','participantId','ownerId','displayName','kind']`; `agent` → those plus `'ownerLabel','harness'`; `unknown` → `['matrixUserId','displayName','kind']`. `matrixUserId` uses `readMatrixUserId`; `participantId` and `ownerId` use `identifier`; `displayName` and `ownerLabel` use `label(…, 512)`; `harness` uses `readHarness`.
- `decodeParticipantsResponse`: at most 100 entries, and a repeated `matrixUserId` fails with `'duplicate'` at its element path.

`inbox.ts`:
- `InboxEntry` and `INBOX_BODY_MAX_BYTES = 65_536`.
- `decodeInboxEntry`:
  - `eventId` uses `identifier` and `/^\$\S+$/u`;
  - `roomId` uses `readRoomId` and `sender` uses `readMatrixUserId`;
  - `ts` uses `utcTimestamp`;
  - `senderLabel` uses `label(…, 512)`;
  - `senderKind` and `kind` use `literal`;
  - `body` uses `text(…, INBOX_BODY_MAX_BYTES)`, so newlines are allowed.
- `encodeInboxLine(entry: InboxEntry): string` returns `JSON.stringify(entry) + '\n'`.
- `decodeInboxLine(line: string): Decoded<InboxEntry>`: invalid JSON gives `{ ok:false, error:{ path:'', code:'invalid_value' } }`.

### Worked example

Input to `decodeAgentJoinRequest`:

```json
{ "link": "https://127.0.0.1:8443/join/inv_abcdefgh", "harness": "claude", "label": "Claude" }
```

Output: `{ ok: true, value: <same object> }`. With `"label": " Claude"`, the output is `{ ok:false, error:{ path:'label', code:'invalid_value' } }`, and `agentJoinRequestErrorCode(error)` is `'invalid_label'`.

Input to `decodeParticipantsResponse`, then output `ok:true`:

```json
{ "participants": [
  { "matrixUserId": "@khala_a2luzw:khala.local", "participantId": "human_<40 hex>", "ownerId": "owner_kevin", "displayName": "Kevin", "kind": "human" },
  { "matrixUserId": "@agent-1a2b3c4d-x9y8z7:khala.local", "participantId": "agent_<40 hex>", "ownerId": "owner_kevin", "displayName": "Claude · Kevin", "kind": "agent", "ownerLabel": "Kevin", "harness": "claude" },
  { "matrixUserId": "@stranger:khala.local", "displayName": "@stranger:khala.local", "kind": "unknown" } ] }
```

`encodeInboxLine` of:

```json
{"eventId":"$e1","roomId":"!r:khala.local","ts":"2026-10-02T10:04:00.000Z","sender":"@khala_a2luzw:khala.local","senderLabel":"Maya","senderKind":"human","kind":"message","body":"Docs are a go from my side."}
```

returns that JSON plus `\n`. `decodeInboxLine` of that line returns the same object.

## Test scenarios

`packages/contracts/src/m1/agent-join.test.ts`:
1. The valid worked-example request → `ok:true`.
2. Label cases → `invalid_label`:
   - `" Claude"` (non-canonical);
   - `""`;
   - 41 characters;
   - `"Khala bot"` (reserved);
   - `"A\u200bB"` (a zero-width space; write it as a `\u200b` escape in the test).
   A label of exactly 40 characters → ok.
3. `harness: "gemini"` → error path `harness`, mapped to `invalid_harness`.
4. Link cases → `invalid_link`:
   - `https://x.test/join/short`;
   - `https://x.test/join/inv_abcdefgh?x=1`;
   - `https://x.test/join/inv_abcdefgh#f`;
   - `https://u:p@x.test/join/inv_abcdefgh`;
   - `http://example.test/join/inv_abcdefgh` (non-loopback http);
   - `https://x.test/room/inv_abcdefgh`.
   `http://127.0.0.1:8888/join/inv_abcdefgh` → ok.
5. An extra key `{…, owner:"x"}` → `unknown_field`, mapped to `invalid_link`.
6. `decodeAgentJoinPoll`:
   - each of the four states decodes;
   - `{state:'pending', credentials:{…}}` fails;
   - `{state:'confirmed'}` fails with `missing_field`.
7. `decodeAgentCredentials` with the contracts.md example values (`https://127.0.0.1:8443`, `@agent-1a2b3c4d-x9y8z7:khala.local`, `KH_AGENT_1a2b3c4d`) → ok. `homeserver: "https://h.test/path"` fails. `roomId: "!opaqueid"` (no server part) → ok.
8. `decodeAgentJoinView` with and without `agentUserId` → ok. The result without it has no `agentUserId` key (`'agentUserId' in value === false`).
9. Each path helper encodes its id:
   - `agentJoinPollPath('a/b')` → `/api/agent/join/poll?joinId=a%2Fb`
   - `humanAgentJoinPath('j1')` → `/api/human/agent-join?joinId=j1`
   - `agentConfirmPagePath('j1')` → `/agent/confirm?joinId=j1`
10. `decodeAgentJoinCreated` with `joinId: "j1"` and `confirmUrl: "https://127.0.0.1:8443/agent/confirm?joinId=j1"` → ok. Each of these `confirmUrl` values fails at path `confirmUrl`:
    - `…/agent/confirm?joinId=j2`
    - `…/agent/confirm/j1`
    - `…/agent/confirm?joinId=j1&x=1`
11. `decodeAgentJoinError({error:'not_found'})` → ok; `{error:'nope'}` → fail.

`packages/contracts/src/m1/participants.test.ts`:
1. The worked-example response → ok.
2. An agent participant missing `ownerLabel` → fail. A human participant with extra `harness` → fail. An `unknown` participant carrying `ownerId` → fail. A human participant without `kind` → fail (`kind` is mandatory in M1).
3. 101 participants → fail. A duplicate `matrixUserId` → `duplicate` at `participants[1]`.
4. `agentOwnerRecordKey('@agent-1a2b3c4d-x9y8z7:khala.local')` → `agents/%40agent-1a2b3c4d-x9y8z7%3Akhala.local`.
5. `decodeAgentOwnerRecord` valid → ok. `createdAt: "yesterday"` fails. `label: "system"` fails.
6. `ownerFirstName` cases:
   - `kevin.weaver2@gmail.com` → `Kevin`
   - `maya@x.test` → `Maya`
   - `bob99@x.test` → `Bob`
   - `ann-marie@x.test` → `Ann`
   - `j_doe@x.test` → `J`
   - `+tag@x.test` → `Owner`
   - `42@x.test` → `Owner`
   - `éva@x.test` → `Éva`

`packages/contracts/src/m1/inbox.test.ts`:
1. Round trip of the worked example through `encodeInboxLine` and `decodeInboxLine`.
2. A body with newlines and `system:` text → ok and unchanged.
3. Each of these fails:
   - `senderKind: "bot"`;
   - `kind: "notice"`;
   - `eventId: "e1"` (no `$`);
   - a body over 65,536 bytes;
   - a body containing `\u0000`.
4. `decodeInboxLine('{not json')` → `{ ok:false, error:{ path:'', code:'invalid_value' } }`.

## Verification

```sh
pnpm --filter @khala/contracts test
pnpm --filter @khala/contracts typecheck
pnpm check:boundaries
pnpm typecheck
```

Done when:
- the three new test files pass;
- typecheck and boundaries are green;
- `grep -n '"./m1/\*"' packages/contracts/package.json` prints exactly one line;
- `git diff --stat` shows no file outside the exclusive write surfaces.

## Risks and stop conditions

- If contracts.md changes C2, C3 or C5 before you start, follow the amended text. Do not reconcile two versions yourself.
- Stop and ask the Executor if `validateAgentName`'s reserved list rejects a default label the agent lane needs, such as `Claude` or `Codex`. Both pass today, but check.
- Do not import `node:*` or anything outside `packages/contracts`, because the boundary check fails.
- The path helpers follow the amended C2: exact paths carrying `?joinId=`, because the gateway matches exact paths only (`apps/control/src/runtime/handler.ts:9-14`). If C2 changes again, follow the newest contracts.md. Do not invent a scheme.

## Complexity rationale

1: three pure modules with no I/O and an existing decode toolkit to follow. The only judgement call is label canonicality, which is settled above.
